verdicts.why: Hostility is the meaning (ill will, ill feeling), a bad referent named plainly; choosing it over 'hostile' adds register, not attitude.
An ill omen is simply an inauspicious one; the word states the foreboding rather than taking a side on it.
Technical sense of representing something by a symbol or formula; no attitude toward the thing expressed.
Plain shipping term for sending by rapid transport; describes a method without judging.
Pressing juice or oil from a substance is a neutral physical process.
Genetics term for a trait being manifested; purely descriptive.
A general idea or impression is one lacking detail; the word describes vagueness of scope without contempt for it.
Worldwide or universal applicability is a matter of scope, not of approval.
Medical sense (general anaesthesia, general paralysis) describing extent over the body; no attitude.
Hiring someone for work is stated plainly; the word carries no view of the hire.
Engaging in battle names the activity without judging the combatants or the cause.
Neutral synonym of hire; no approval or contempt attaches to the person engaged.
Contracting for service is a plain transactional term.
Keeping gears, attention, or a person occupied is described without any stance toward it.
Retaining legal counsel is a neutral procedural act.
Mechanical sense of parts catching or meshing; nothing to judge.
Grammatical term for the constituent acted upon; wholly technical.
Computing term for a data item; no attitude possible.
Names a supernatural being without the speaker taking a side on it, unlike a word such as 'spook'.
The animating principle of a character or age is named descriptively; approval belongs to the modifier (a generous spirit), not the noun.
The prevailing atmosphere of a place or occasion is described neutrally; it can be good or bad.
The intended meaning as opposed to the letter is a plain distinction, not an evaluation.
A spirit of adventure or of rebellion is a tendency named without the noun itself praising or blaming it.
Saying something will answer means it suffices; a plain statement of adequacy with no attitude beyond that.
Answering a purpose or requirement is a neutral functional claim, not a judgement of what is served.
